assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original pixel-art sprite animation sheet for an existing side-view browser action platformer.
Input images: Image 1 is the identity, costume and pixel-art style reference for the three existing enemies; Image 2 is a supporting reference for their body proportions and texture. Do not recreate these sheets: create a new attack-animation sheet.
Primary request: exactly 24 separate complete-body poses in a spacious 4-column by 6-row grid, read left-to-right row-by-row. Every character faces RIGHT, side view, feet consistently registered per row. All silhouettes fully inside their cells, generous empty separation, no labels, no UI, no shadows under feet, no detached particles. Background perfectly solid magenta #ff00ff for the game's established chroma-key import.
Rows 1-2: SAME gaunt soaked man in petrol-green torn municipal coat, amber eyes, boots, dark trousers as reference. Eight sequential poses of ONE readable forward claw strike: row 1 progresses through (1) slight alert shoulder lift (2) turn torso with elbow drawing back (3) knees braced, claw hand high behind shoulder (4) strongest anticipatory coil. Row 2: (5) forward open-hand thrust at chest height (6) fully extended forward downward follow-through (7) bent over, elbow returns (8) nearly neutral exhausted stance. The attack only reaches in front, never swings backwards.
Rows 3-4: SAME violet-hooded spitter, grey face, amber eye, long ragged raincoat. Row 3 four consecutive full-body anticipation poses: straighten slightly, hand rises toward throat, shoulders swell and mouth opens, lean back ready to spit. Row 4: two forward spitting body poses WITHOUT drawn projectile or spray; then two recoil-to-neutral recovery poses.
Rows 5-6: SAME black asphalt-matted hound, warm amber eyes, coarse wet fur. Row 5 four poses progressively coiling toward a pounce: ears pin back, shoulders lower, knees fold deeper, fully compressed crouch. Row 6: two forward leaping bite poses (gathered limbs then extended limbs), landing/compressed forelegs, then rising into alert stance.
Style: crisp authored 16-bit pixel clusters and controlled highlights, no smooth painting or anti-aliased linework. Preserve reference clothes, faces, anatomy, palette and realistic grim proportions. Strengthen the full-body silhouette and shoulder/hip/weight shifts so preparation reads at about 40px character height. Consistent scale across each creature's eight poses; crouching poses must not be enlarged to fill cells. No extra creatures, limbs, props, weapons, text, borders, blur, glow or perspective rotation. Wide enough gutters for every extended arm and tail.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: 12-frame pixel-art enemy collapse animation sheet for the existing side-scrolling game.
Input image: identity/style reference only, depicting three existing enemies. Generate a NEW sheet; preserve every creature's identity, costume, palette and crisp 16-bit pixel-cluster technique.
Composition: exactly 4 columns and 3 rows, reading left to right. One complete creature per cell, full body visible with generous spacing. Consistent scale within a row; a fallen pose must remain short, not enlarged to fill its cell. Feet/ground contact lie on the same baseline in each row. All creatures oriented RIGHT. Solid magenta #ff00ff background, no cast shadows, no ground, no detached particles, no text or borders.
Row 1 is the petrol-green ragged-coat grey-faced municipal walker. Four successive defeated poses: (1) recoils and knees buckle, hand near torso (2) falls to one knee, head drops and hand reaches to support weight (3) shoulder and side reach ground, coat folds beneath him (4) lies still on his side, head to the right, legs bent, complete coat and boots visible.
Row 2 is the SAME violet-hooded grey-faced spitter. Four analogous successive collapse poses: buckling, kneeling, falling onto forearm/side, lying still with hood and coat pooled around the body, head to the right.
Row 3 is the SAME black wet asphalt-matted hound with amber eyes. Four successive poses: (1) startled recoil, forelegs buckle (2) chest lowers with hindquarters still raised (3) falls onto side with legs tucking (4) lies still on its side, head to the right, tail behind.
Restrained non-graphic defeat, NO blood or wounds, no dismemberment or skeleton changes. Full-body motion, not a standing sprite rotated. Same grim realistic anatomy and muted palette as the reference. Compact readable silhouettes at about 40-pixel gameplay height. No glow or blurs. No additional props or creatures. Keep all prone poses wholly inside their own cells.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: four-frame pixel-art collapse animation of the existing port boss.
Input image is identity and costume reference only. Create a NEW wide sprite sheet, exactly FOUR separate full-body poses in ONE horizontal row. Same imposing dock foreman, petrol-blue wet heavy coat, rope belt, brass hard hat, dark face with amber eyes, gloves, boots and the same rusty anchor. All four oriented RIGHT. Preserve all identity, palette and proportions. Crisp 16-bit pixel clusters, not smooth illustration.
Four sequential non-graphic defeat poses: (1) both knees buckle, shoulder slumps while the anchor lowers to the ground, (2) down on one knee and supported by one glove, anchor resting beside him, (3) falling onto his side, coat bunching, helmet stays on, anchor touching his hand and lying on the ground, (4) lying still on his side with head toward the right, heavy coat and boots visible, anchor lying next to and touching the body so the entire silhouette is one connected cluster.
Solid flat magenta #ff00ff background. Same apparent scale and same ground baseline across all four cells. Do not enlarge the fallen poses to fill their cells. Generous wide gutters and enough room for the complete prone body and anchor, nothing cropped, no overlap between cells. No cast shadows, no background scenery, no blood, gore, particles, text, frame numbers, logos or borders. Genuine full-body drawing for every pose, never just rotate the standing character.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: final full-body boss animation sheet for a gloomy contemporary Batumi 2D pixel action platformer.
References: Image 1 gives the identity, anatomy, clothing, giant anchor weapon and pixel style of the existing port foreman boss. Image 2 supports the same clothing and helmet details, NOT the death poses. Create NEW attack poses, not a copy of either sheet.
Exactly SIXTEEN distinct complete-body figures in a generous FOUR COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS grid, read left to right. Every figure faces RIGHT. Keep all boots, helmet, hands, coat, anchor and attached chain connected within one complete silhouette. The chain must remain visibly connected to hand and anchor. Perfectly solid bright magenta #ff00ff background. Empty gutters, no shadows, no text, no UI, no gridlines, no particles or detached glowing effects.
The SAME imposing drowned dock foreman in every cell: brass hardhat, grey face, dark facial hair, oversized petroleum-green weathered raincoat with circular anchor badge, heavy brown boots, thick gloves, bulky worn iron anchor gripped as weapon. Contemporary ghost dockworker, no medieval armor, no cape, no exposed gore.
Rows 1-2 together depict ONE eight-pose grounded forward anchor slam, ALL FACING RIGHT:
Row1: (1) boots brace wide, both hands begin drawing anchor close; (2) deep torso turn, elbows draw anchor shaft up toward shoulder; (3) knees flex and anchor rises above/behind the right-facing shoulder; (4) maximum coiled anticipation, massive anchor held overhead, unmistakably ready to slam forward. Keep chain anchored, no detached links.
Row2: (5) powerful forward descending anchor swing, torso and knees follow through; (6) anchor head visibly planted on ground in front/right of boots with body leaning forward; (7) slow exhausted pull upward with both arms and one knee braced; (8) nearly recovered forward-facing ready stance, anchor resting beside forward boot.
Rows 3-4 together depict ONE eight-pose supernatural forward signal/volley cast (no actual projectiles drawn; game draws them):
Row3: (9) anchor held low near the rear boot, free hand rises toward chest; (10) helmeted head and torso pull back, open palm close to sternum; (11) bent knees, shoulders gathered, casting arm coils; (12) greatest anticipatory tension, palm drawn back ready to push forward. Row4: (13) palm thrust fully forward RIGHT at chest height, anchor still in opposite hand low; (14) body leans into the completed thrust, fingers extended toward RIGHT; (15) wrist drops and shoulders sag into recovery; (16) upright settled stance, anchor at rest.
Crisp authored 16-bit pixel clusters, restrained cool stone/teal shadows and brass accents. Full-body anatomy shifts and readable shoulder/hip silhouettes, consistent scale across all16 poses. Do not stretch crouched poses to fill their cells. Boots share a stable per-row baseline. Final display standing height about70 logical pixels. No smooth painting, motion blur, redrawn line limbs, extra hands, duplicate anchor heads, extra figures, captions, or environment. Preserve recognizability of the exact reference boss.
